findings.title: Task 9.4 writes a merge as a task item
findings.description: Task 9.4 tells the implementer to merge the slice branch into the target. Task 9's success criteria also say "committed/merged". The project Git Rules say never to write a merge or push as a task, sub-item, or success criterion. Merging happens only in Phase 7 (Slice Integration), after code review passes. A junior implementer following this file would merge before review. Remove 9.4 and the "merged" wording. Task 9 should end with the commit on the slice branch. The Branch note about forking from the integration target is fine to keep.

findings.title: Task 5.2 needs a fake-server capability that Task 3 does not build
findings.description: The timeout test must prove the child process is gone. Task 5.2 suggests having the fake server "print its PID to a temp file at startup". Task 3.1 defines only the `echo`, `fail`, `sleep` and `empty` tools. Task 3.2's helper has no way to pass a PID-file path to the server. Task 5 would therefore have to edit the Task 3 fixture, which breaks the "infrastructure first" ordering. Choose one mechanism and move it into Task 3. For example, the fake server writes `os.getpid()` to a path taken from an env var or argument, and the 3.2 helper accepts that path. Task 5.2 would then only read it.

findings.title: Two failure and mapping paths are implemented but never tested
findings.description:
The slice says "Each row above has a test asserting the observable signal" for its failure-mode table. The task file leaves two gaps:
- **Protocol/transport error:** Task 4.3 implements the `McpError` and closed-stream path with a WARNING. No Task 5 test triggers it. The fake server has no tool that crashes or exits mid-call. A small `crash` tool that calls `os._exit` would cover it, and Task 3 and Task 5 would need to add it.
- **Non-text content blocks:** Task 4.2 requires non-text blocks to be "noted by type in the content", and the slice's Result mapping section requires the same. No fake tool returns an image or other non-text block, and no test asserts the note. The guard against silently dropping content is therefore unverified.

Add these to Tasks 3 and 5, or state explicitly that they are intentionally untested. Nothing in the task file says that today.

findings.title: Tasks 1 and 2 are too granular and should be merged
findings.description: Task 1 adds two config-key entries, and Task 2 adds two default-value assertions. Both are effort 1/5 and together cover a few lines. This produces two commits for one trivial unit. The test-with pattern is better served by one task: add the keys and their default tests, then make one commit. The same file lists no `**Commit**:` markers, and the project rule commits at the end of each top-level task when there are none. Merging therefore also removes a needless commit.

findings.title: Task 3's rationale names the wrong dependent tasks
findings.description: "Tasks 5, 6 both need a real stdio peer" is inaccurate. Task 6 builds `cf_tools.py`, and Task 7 mocks the transport. The real consumers of the fixture are Task 5 (the bridge tests) and the Task 4 smoke check. Fix the wording so the dependency graph stays trustworthy.

findings.title: Success criterion 6 is only partly closed
findings.description: The slice's criterion 6 includes a dispatch with a tool-capable non-SDK model calling `cf_build_context`, which is walkthrough step 4. Task 9 runs steps 1–3 and leaves step 4 open, citing the CLAUDECODE guard. This is reasonable and disclosed. Note, though, that criterion 6 will remain unmet at close-out. The task file marks the slice `status: complete`, which slightly overstates that. Consider phrasing the status or DEVLOG entry so the open demo is explicit.
